dstask

Single binary terminal-based TODO manager with git-based sync + markdown notes per task




Dstask is a personal task tracker designed to help you focus. It is similar to [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) but uses git to synchronise instead of a special protocol. If you're at home in the terminal, and with solving the occasional merge conflict, then dstask is for you! https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/589d06fd-7486-46e4-b838-ce85af12f0fc [Video courtesy of xGoivo -- thanks!](https://www.reddit.com/r/taskwarrior/comments/1o7itzg/what_do_you_guys_think_about_this_taskwarrior/) ## Features - Powerful context system (automatically applies filter/tags to queries and new tasks) - **Git powered sync**/undo/resolve ([passwordstore.org](https://www.passwordstore.org/) style) which means no need to set up a sync server, and syncing between devices is easy! - Task listing won't break with long task text - `note` command -- edit a **full markdown note** for each task. **Checklists are useful here.** - `open` command -- **open URLs found in specified task** (including notes) in the browser - zsh/bash completion (including tags and projects in current context) for speed; PowerShell completion on Windows - A single statically-linked binary - import tool which can import GitHub issues or taskwarrior tasks. ## Non-features - Collaboration. This is a personal task tracker. Use another system for projects that involve multiple people. Note that it can still be beneficial to use dstask to track what you are working on in the context of a multi-person project tracked elsewhere. ## Requirements - Git - A 256-color capable terminal ## Installation 1. Copy the executable (from the [releases page][releases]) to somewhere in your PATH. - Linux/macOS: name it `dstask` and mark it executable (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/`). - Windows: use `dstask.exe` and place it in a directory on `PATH` (e.g. `%USERPROFILE%\bin`). 1. Enable shell completions: - Bash: add `source <(dstask bash-completion)` to your `.bashrc`. - Zsh: add `dstask zsh-completion > /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_dstask` or source completions in your `~/.zshrc`. - PowerShell (Windows): see section "PowerShell completion" below. 1. Set up an alias in your `.bashrc`: `alias task=dstask` or `alias t=dstask` to make task management slightly faster. 1. Create or clone a `~/.dstask` git repository for the data, if you haven't already: - Linux/macOS: `mkdir ~/.dstask && git -C ~/.dstask init` - Windows: `mkdir %USERPROFILE%\.dstask && git -C %USERPROFILE%\.dstask init` ## PowerShell completion Save the completion script to a file and source it in your PowerShell profile: ```powershell dstask powershell-completion > ~\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\dstask-completion.ps1 Add-Content $PROFILE '. ~/Documents/WindowsPowerShell/dstask-completion.ps1' ``` ## Usage Run `dstask help` for usage information. ### Basic Commands - `dstask add [tags] [project:name] [priority:P0-P3]` - Add a new task - `dstask` or `dstask next` - Show next tasks to work on - `dstask start` - Start working on a task - `dstask stop` - Stop working on a task - `dstask done` - Mark a task as complete - `dstask edit` - Edit a task - `dstask note` - Edit the markdown note for a task - `dstask open` - Open URLs in task and note - `dstask show-open` - Show all open tasks - `dstask show-resolved` - Show completed tasks - `dstask show-paused` - Show paused tasks - `dstask context ` - Switch to a context (filter) - `dstask sync` - Synchronise with git remote ### Task Properties - **Priority**: P0 (highest), P1, P2 (default), P3 (lowest) - **Tags**: Add with `+tag`, remove with `-tag` - **Projects**: Set with `project:name` - **Due dates**: Set with `due:YYYY-MM-DD` - **Status**: open, active, paused, resolved ### Contexts Contexts automatically filter tasks and apply tags to new tasks: ```bash dstask context work dstask add finish report # automatically tagged with +work dstask # shows only work tasks dstask context -- # clear context ``` ### Git Sync Sync your tasks across devices using git: ```bash # Set up sync on first device cd ~/.dstask git remote add origin git push -u origin master # On other devices git clone ~/.dstask # To sync dstask sync ``` ### Templates Create task templates for recurring patterns: ```bash dstask add template +template project:meetings priority:P1 dstask add from-template ``` ## Best Practices - Create contexts for different areas of your life (work, home, etc.) to maintain focus. - Use tags liberally to categorize tasks, but avoid tag explosion. Use 3-5 tags per task at most. - Keep ta 1982 characters elided (( $# == 1 || has_double_dash )) && \ [[ "${subcommand}" =~ ^(done|edit|note|open|remove|start|stop)$ ]] then command dstask show-open $( (( has_double_dash )) && echo "--" ) \ | jq -r '.[] | [.id, .summary] | @tsv' \ | fzf --delimiter='\t' --nth=2 --accept-nth=1 --preview='DSTASK_FAKE_PTY=1 dstask {1} --' \ | xargs -n1 dstask "${subcommand}" return fi fi command dstask "$@" } ``` The wrapper function checks if dstask was called with a subcommand missing the task ID, and if so uses the `show-open` command to get a list of tasks to choose from. `--` can be used to ignore the current context for the fuzzy search. All other commands are passed directly to dstask. ## Alternatives Alternatives listed must be capable of running in the terminal. - [TaskLite](https://github.com/ad-si/TaskLite) -- The CLI task manager for power users, written in Haskell - [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) -- the closest analogue - [Taskbook](https://github.com/klaussinani/taskbook) -- board metaphor, note support - [todo.txt-cli](https://github.com/todotxt/todo.txt-cli) - [etm](https://github.com/dagraham/etm-dgraham) -- event and task manager - [t](https://github.com/sjl/t) -- a minimal todo list with an amusing philosophy ## FAQ > Does dstask encrypt tasks? Encryption is not a design goal of dstask. If you want to have your remote repository encrypted, you may consider [git-remote-gcrypt](https://spwhitton.name/tech/code/git-remote-gcrypt/) or [git-crypt](https://github.com/AGWA/git-crypt). Note that dstask has not been tested with these tools, nor can any claims be made about the security of the tools themselves. > Is it possible to modify more than one task at once with a filter? Yes. 1. Set a context: 2. Run a modify command without and ID 3. Hit y to confirm to modify all tasks in context This means it's natural to review the tasks that would be modified before modifying by listing all tasks in the current context first, instead of potentially operating blindly by matching tags or numbers. You can also specify multiple task numbers at one time, as with any other command. > Is there a GUI or web interface? Not as part of dstask itself. However, dstask can be used as a library -- @botto has started developing a web GUI, specifically to allow task management on-the-go via a smartphone: . It's in early stages but is meaningful as having no smartphone-based control is a blocker for a lot of people. > Has dstask been featured in a magazine? Yes! :-) [releases]: https://github.com/naggie/dstask/releases --- dstask-import --- # dstask-import usage: `dstask-import github|tw` dstask-import is a tool to synchronize between external services or tools, and dstask. At this point it supports importing from: * taskwarrior * GitHub See below for details on each ## Taskwarrior The import functionality is designed to aid with the transition from using taskwarrior to dstask. Before installing dstask, you may want to export your taskwarrior database: task export > taskwarrior.json After un-installing taskwarrior and installing dstask, to import the tasks to dstask after initialising the dstask database with git: mkdir ~/.dstask && git -C ~/.dstask init dstask-import tw < taskwarrior.json Note that the import process is lossy due to subtle differences between taskwarrior and dstask. ## GitHub You can import issues from GitHub repositories into dstask. ### Authentication To import from private repositories, you'll need a GitHub personal access token. For public repositories, authentication is optional but recommended to avoid rate limits. ### Usage To import issues from a GitHub repository: dstask-import github / You can also import from multiple repositories by running the command multiple times. --- taskwarrior-migration --- # Moving from Taskwarrior ## Importing data Please see the [dstask-import tw instructions](dstask-import.md#taskwarrior) to import taskwarrior tasks. ## Using dstask Commands and syntax are deliberately very similar to taskwarrior. Here are the exceptions: * The command is (nearly) always the first argument. Eg, `task eat some add bananas` won't work, but `task add eat some bananas` will. If there's an ID, it can proceed the command but doesn't have to. * Priorities are added by the keywords `P0` `P1` `P2` `P3`. Lower number is more urgent. Default is `P2`. For example `task add eat some bananas P1`. The keyword can be anywhere after the command. * Action is always the first argument. Eg, `task eat some add bananas` won't work, but `task add eat some bananas` will. * Contexts are defined on-the-fly, and are added to all new tasks if set. Create task templates for recurring patterns:

```bash
dstask add template +template project:meetings priority:P1
dstask add from-template <template-id>
```

## Best Practices

- Create contexts for different areas of your life (work, home, etc.) to maintain focus.
- Use tags liberally to categorize tasks, but avoid tag explosion. Use 3-5 tags per task at most.
- Keep task summaries brief. Use the note field for details, checklists, and context.
- Use dstask to track things you might forget, rather than everything. SNR is important. Don't track tasks for the sake of it, and don't track _ideas_. Track ideas separately.
- Spend regular time reviewing tasks. You'll probably find some you've already resolved, and many you've forgotten. The `show-unorganised` command is good for this.
- Try to work through tasks from the top of the list. Dstask sorts by priority then creation date -- the most important tasks are at the top.
- Use `start`/`stop` to mark what you're genuinely working on right now; it makes resuming work faster. Paused tasks will be slightly highlighted, so you won't lose track of them. `show-paused` helps if they start to pile up.
- Keep a [github-style check list](https://help.github.com/en/articles/about-task-lists) in the markdown note of complex or procedural tasks
- Failing to get started working? Start with the smallest task
- Record only required tasks. Track ideas separately, else your task list will grow unboundedly!
- set `DSTASK_CONTEXT` in a `.envrc` per-project repository. With direnv, this allows you to automatically switch context

## Database

The default database location is:

- Linux/macOS: `~/.dstask/`
- Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.dstask`

It can be configured by the environment variable `DSTASK_GIT_REPO`.

## Integration of fuzzy finders

Instead of passing task IDs to commands, a fuzzy finder like [*fzf*](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) can be used to
search tasks by their summary instead. This is not part of dstask itself, but can be achieved by defining a shell
wrapper like this in your `.bashrc` or `.zshrc`:

```bash
function dstask () {
    local has_double_dash subcommand

    if (( $# == 1 || $# == 2 )); then
        has_double_dash="$( [[ "$1" == "--" || "$2" == "--" ]] && echo "1" || echo "0" )"
        subcommand="$( [[ "$1" == "--" ]] && echo "$2" || echo "$1" )"
        if (( $# == 1 || has_double_dash )) && \
            [[ "${subcommand}" =~ ^(done|edit|note|open|remove|start|stop)$ ]]
        then
            command dstask show-open $( (( has_double_dash )) && echo "--" ) \
                | jq -r '.[] | [.id, .summary] | @tsv' \
                | fzf --delimiter='\t' --nth=2 --accept-nth=1 --preview='DSTASK_FAKE_PTY=1 dstask {1} --' \
                | xargs -n1 dstask "${subcommand}"
            return
        fi
    fi

    command dstask "$@"
}
```

The wrapper function checks if dstask was called with a subcommand missing the task ID, and if so uses the `show-open`
command to get a list of tasks to choose from. `--` can be used to ignore the current context for the fuzzy search. All
other commands are passed directly to dstask.

## Alternatives

Alternatives listed must be capable of running in the terminal.

- [TaskLite](https://github.com/ad-si/TaskLite) -- The CLI task manager for power users, written in Haskell
- [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) -- the closest analogue
- [Taskbook](https://github.com/klaussinani/taskbook) -- board metaphor, note support
- [todo.txt-cli](https://github.com/todotxt/todo.txt-cli)
- [etm](https://github.com/dagraham/etm-dgraham) -- event and task manager
- [t](https://github.com/sjl/t) -- a minimal todo list with an amusing philosophy

## FAQ

> Does dstask encrypt tasks?

Encryption is not a design goal of dstask. If you want to have your remote
repository encrypted, you may consider
[git-remote-gcrypt](https://spwhitton.name/tech/code/git-remote-gcrypt/) or
[git-crypt](https://github.com/AGWA/git-crypt). Note that dstask has not been
tested with these tools, nor can any claims be made about the security of the
tools themselves.

> Is it possible to modify more than one task at once with a filter?

Yes.

1. Set a context:
2. Run a modify command without and ID
3. Hit y to confirm to modify all tasks in context

This means it's natural to review the tasks that would be modified before
modifying by listing all tasks in the current context first, instead of
potentially operating blindly by matching tags or numbers.

You can also specify multiple task numbers at one time, as with any other command.

> Is there a GUI or web interface?

Not as part of dstask itself. However, dstask can be used as a library -- @botto
has started developing a web GUI, specifically to allow task management on-the-go
via a smartphone: <https://github.com/botto/dstask-gui> . It's in early stages but
is meaningful as having no smartphone-based control is a blocker for a lot of people.

> Has dstask been featured in a magazine?

Yes! <https://www.linux-magazine.com/Issues/2021/246/dstask> :-)

===bash-completion===
# wire bash completions to dstask completion engine. Some of the workarounds for
# idiosyncrasies around separation with colons taken from /etc/bash_completion

_dstask() {
    # reconstruct COMP_WORDS to re-join separations caused by colon (which is a default separator)
    # yes, this method ends up splitting by spaces, but that's not a problem for the dstask parser
    # see http://tiswww.case.edu/php/chet/bash/FAQ
    original_args=( $(echo "${COMP_WORDS[@]}" | sed 's/ : /:/g' | sed 's/ :$/:/g') )

    # hand to dstask as canonical args
    COMPREPLY=( $(dstask _completions "${original_args[@]}") )

    # convert dstask's suggestions to remove prefix before colon so complete can understand it
    local last_arg="${original_args[-1]}"
    local colon_word=${last_arg%"${last_arg##*:}"}
    local i=${#COMPREPLY[*]}
    while [[ $((--i)) -ge 0 ]]; do
        COMPREPLY[$i]=${COMPREPLY[$i]#"$colon_word"}
    done
}

def eprint_red(msg):

def now_rfc3339nano():
    ns = time_ns()
    sec = ns // 1_000_000_000
    nsec = ns % 1_000_000_000
    dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(sec, tz=timezone.utc)
    if nsec == 0:
        return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    frac = f"{nsec:09d}".rstrip("0")
    return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S") + f".{frac}Z"


def time_ns():
    try:
        return __import__('time').time_ns()
    except AttributeError:
        return int(__import__('time').time() * 1_000_000_000)


def date_to_rfc(d: date):
    return d.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00Z")


def parse_rfc_date(s):
    if not s or s == ZERO_TIME:
        return None
    try:
        return datetime.strptime(s[:10], "%Y-%m-%d").date()
    except Exception:
        return None


def sorted_unique(vals):
    return sorted(set([v for v in vals if v]))


def shell_quote_yaml(s):
    # The original YAML is mostly plain scalars. Quote only cases that would be
    # ambiguous for our small parser/YAML readers.
    if s == "":
        return '""'
    if s.strip() != s or s.startswith(('-', '{', '[', '#', '&', '*', '!', '|', '>', '@', '`')):
        return json.dumps(s)
    if "\n" in s:
        return json.dumps(s)
    if s.lower() in ("null", "true", "false", "yes", "no"):
        return json.dumps(s)
    return s


def yaml_unquote(s):
    s = s.rstrip("\n")
    if s == '""':
        return ""
    if len(s) >= 2 and s[0] == '"' and s[-1] == '"':
        try:
            return json.loads(s)
        except Exception:
            return s[1:-1]
    return s


def write_task(repo: Path, t: Task):
    d = repo / t.status
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p = d / f"{t.uuid}.yml"
    old = getattr(t, 'path', None)
    if old and Path(old) != p and Path(old).exists():
        try:
            Path(old).unlink()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"summary: {shell_quote_yaml(t.summary)}\n")
    notes = t.notes if t.notes is not None else ""
    if notes == "":
        lines.append('notes: ""\n')
    elif "\n" in notes:
        # Choose chomp indicator similar to Go yaml.v2: trailing newline => |, otherwise |-
        indicator = "|" if notes.endswith("\n") else "|-"
        # If string starts with a newline, yaml.v2 emits |2-
        if notes.startswith("\n") and not notes.endswith("\n"):
            indicator = "|2-"
        lines.append(f"notes: {indicator}\n")
        for line in notes.split("\n"):
            # For a final trailing newline split gives an empty last element; yaml | does not need an
            # explicit final blank line.
            if line == "" and line is notes.split("\n")[-1]:
                continue
        parts = notes.split("\n")
        if notes.endswith("\n"):
            parts = parts[:-1]
        for line in parts:
            lines.append(f"  {line}\n")
    else:
        lines.append(f"notes: {shell_quote_yaml(notes)}\n")
    tags = sorted_unique(t.tags)
    if tags:
        lines.append("tags:\n")
        for tag in tags:
            lines.append(f"- {tag}\n")
    else:
        lines.append("tags: []\n")
    lines.append(f"project: {shell_quote_yaml(t.project)}\n")
    lines.append(f"priority: {t.priority or 'P2'}\n")
    lines.append('delegatedto: ""\n')
    lines.append("subtasks: []\n")
    lines.append("dependencies: []\n")
    lines.append(f"created: {t.created}\n")
    lines.append(f"resolved: {t.resolved}\n")
    lines.append(f"due: {t.due}\n")
    p.write_text("".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
    t.path = p


def parse_task_file(path: Path, status: str):
    data = {
        "summary": "", "notes": "", "tags": [], "project": "", "priority": "P2",
        "delegatedto": "", "subtasks": [], "dependencies": [],
        "created": ZERO_TIME, "resolved": ZERO_TIME, "due": ZERO_TIME,
    }
    try:
        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        lines = path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith('#'):
            i += 1; continue
        if ':' not in line:
            i += 1; continue
        key, val = line.split(':', 1)
        key = key.strip()
        val = val.lstrip()
        if key == "status":
            if val:
                status = yaml_unquote(val)
            i += 1; continue
        if key == "tags":
            tags = []
            if val.strip() == "[]":
                i += 1
            elif val.strip():
                # crude inline list support
                v = val.strip()
                if v.startswith('[') and v.endswith(']'):
                    inner = v[1:-1].strip()
                    if inner:
                        tags = [yaml_unquote(x.strip()) for x in inner.split(',')]
                i += 1
            else:
                i += 1
                while i < len(lines) and (lines[i].startswith('- ') or lines[i].startswith('  - ')):
                    item = lines[i].split('-', 1)[1].strip()
                    tags.append(yaml_unquote(item))
                    i += 1
            data["tags"] = sorted_unique(tags)
            continue
        if key == "notes" and val.startswith('|'):
            indicator = val
            i += 1
            note_lines = []
            while i < len(lines) and (lines[i].startswith(' ') or lines[i] == ''):
                l = lines[i]
                if l.startswith('  '):
                    l = l[2:]
                elif l.startswith(' '):
                    l = l[1:]
                note_lines.append(l)
                i += 1
            txt = "\n".join(note_lines)
            if indicator.strip() == "|":
                txt += "\n"
            data["notes"] = txt
            continue
        if key in data:
            data[key] = yaml_unquote(val)
        i += 1
    return Task(
        uuid=path.stem, status=status, summary=data.get("summary", ""), notes=data.get("notes", ""),
        tags=sorted_unique(data.get("tags", [])), project=data.get("project", ""),
        priority=data.get("priority", "P2") or "P2", created=str(data.get("created", ZERO_TIME)),
        resolved=str(data.get("resolved", ZERO_TIME)), due=str(data.get("due", ZERO_TIME)),
        path=path, delegatedto=data.get("delegatedto", ""),
    )


def repo_path():
    return Path(os.environ.get("DSTASK_GIT_REPO") or (Path.home() / ".dstask"))


def ensure_repo():
    repo = repo_path()
    if repo.exists():
        if not (repo / ".git").exists():
            eprint_red("Failed to create directory in git repository")
            sys.exit(1)
    else:
        repo.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        proc = subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=str(repo), text=True, capture_output=True)
        if proc.stdout:
            sys.stdout.write(proc.stdout)
        if proc.stderr:
            sys.stderr.write(proc.stderr)
        print("\nAdd a remote repository with:\n\n\tdstask git remote add origin <repo>\n")
    # create status dirs lazily only when writing; original doesn't create them on list
    return repo


def git_cmd(repo: Path, args, capture=False):
    if capture:
        return subprocess.run(["git"] + args, cwd=str(repo), text=True, capture_output=True)
    return subprocess.run(["git"] + args, cwd=str(repo), text=True)


def run_git_passthrough(repo: Path, args):
    proc = git_cmd(repo, args)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        eprint_red("Failed to run git cmd.")
        return 1
    return 0


def commit_all(repo: Path, message: str):
    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "--all"], cwd=str(repo), text=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    proc = subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=str(repo), text=True, capture_output=True)
    sys.stdout.write(GREY)
    if proc.stdout:
        sys.stdout.write(proc.stdout)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        if proc.stderr:
            sys.stderr.write(proc.stderr)
        # git's no-change message depends on version; original normalizes it.
        combined = (proc.stdout or "") + (proc.stderr or "")
        if "nothing to commit" in combined or "no changes added" in combined or "nothing added to commit" in combined:
            sys.stdout.write("No changes detected\n")
            sys.stdout.write(RESET)
            return 0
        sys.stdout.write(RESET)
        eprint_red(f"error: failed to commit changes: exit status {proc.returncode}")
        return proc.returncode
    sys.stdout.write(RESET)
    return 0


def load_tasks(repo: Path):
    tasks = []
    for status in STATUS_DIRS:
        d = repo / status
        if not d.is_dir():
            continue
        for p in sorted(d.glob("*.yml")):
            tasks.append(parse_task_file(p, status))
    assign_ids(repo, tasks)
    return tasks


def state_dir(repo: Path):
    d = repo / ".git" / "dstask_py"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def ids_file(repo: Path):
    return state_dir(repo) / "ids.json"


def read_ids(repo: Path):
    p = ids_file(repo)
    if not p.exists():
        return {}
    try:
        data = json.loads(p.read_text())
        return {str(k): int(v) for k, v in data.items()}
    except Exception:
        return {}


def write_ids(repo: Path, mapping):
    p = ids_file(repo)
    p.write_text(json.dumps(mapping, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")


def assign_ids(repo: Path, tasks):
    mapping = read_ids(repo)
    live = {t.uuid for t in tasks if t.status in LIVE_STATUSES}
    mapping = {u: i for u, i in mapping.items() if u in live}
    used = set(mapping.values())
    # Existing live tasks with no ID get the lowest unused integer, in creation order.
    for t in sorted([x for x in tasks if x.status in LIVE_STATUSES], key=lambda x: (parse_time_key(x.created), x.uuid)):
        if t.uuid not in mapping:
            n = 1
            while n in used:
                n += 1
            mapping[t.uuid] = n
            used.add(n)
    for t in tasks:
        t.id = mapping.get(t.uuid, 0) if t.status in LIVE_STATUSES else 0
    write_ids(repo, mapping)


def allocate_id(repo: Path, uuid: str):
    mapping = read_ids(repo)
    # Caller should already have pruned by load_tasks, but do it again roughly.
    used = set(mapping.values())
    n = 1
    while n in used:
        n += 1
    mapping[uuid] = n
    write_ids(repo, mapping)
    return n


def remove_id(repo: Path, uuid: str):
    mapping = read_ids(repo)
    if uuid in mapping:
        del mapping[uuid]
        write_ids(repo, mapping)


def parse_time_key(s):
    if not s or s == ZERO_TIME:
        return datetime.min.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    try:
        ss = s.replace("Z", "+00:00")
        # Python supports up to microseconds; trim nanoseconds for sorting.
        if '.' in ss:
            base, rest = ss.split('.', 1)
            frac = rest.split('+', 1)[0]
            tz = '+00:00' if '+' in rest else ''
            ss = base + '.' + frac[:6].ljust(6, '0') + tz
        return datetime.fromisoformat(ss)
    except Exception:
        return datetime.min.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def sort_tasks(tasks):
    prio = {p:i for i,p in enumerate(PRIORITIES)}
    return sorted(tasks, key=lambda t: (prio.get(t.priority, 2), parse_time_key(t.created), t.uuid))


@dataclass
class Query:
    tags: list = field(default_factory=list)
    antitags: list = field(default_factory=list)
    project: str = ""
    antiprojects: list = field(default_factory=list)
    priority: str = ""
    due: str = ""
    text: str = ""
    template_id: int = 0
    note: str = ""
    ignore_context: bool = False
    ids: list = field(default_factory=list)


def parse_due_token(tok):
    raw = tok
    today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()
    low = raw.lower()
    if low == "today":
        return date_to_rfc(today)
    if low == "tomorrow":
        return date_to_rfc(today + timedelta(days=1))
    if low == "yesterday":
        return date_to_rfc(today - timedelta(days=1))
    weekdays = {
        "monday":0, "mon":0, "tuesday":1, "tue":1, "wednesday":2, "wed":2,
        "thursday":3, "thu":3, "friday":4, "fri":4, "saturday":5, "sat":5,
        "sunday":6, "sun":6,
    }
    next_prefix = False
    name = low
    if low.startswith("next-"):
        next_prefix = True
        name = low[5:]
    if name in weekdays:
        delta = (weekdays[name] - today.weekday()) % 7
        if next_prefix and delta == 0:
            delta = 7
        elif next_prefix:
            delta += 7 if delta == 0 else 0
            # original next-fri from Thursday is eight days? Observed next-fri -> 2026-05-15.
            # That is +8, i.e. always following week's weekday.
            delta = ((weekdays[name] - today.weekday()) % 7) + 7
            if delta == 14:
                delta = 7
        return date_to_rfc(today + timedelta(days=delta))
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{1,2}-\d{1,2}", raw):
        try:
            y,m,d = [int(x) for x in raw.split('-')]
            return date_to_rfc(date(y,m,d))
        except Exception:
            pass
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,2}-\d{1,2}", raw):
        try:
            m,d = [int(x) for x in raw.split('-')]
            return date_to_rfc(date(today.year,m,d))
        except Exception:
            pass
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,2}", raw):
        try:
            d = int(raw)
            return date_to_rfc(date(today.year,today.month,d))
        except Exception:
            pass
    raise ValueError(raw)


def parse_tokens(tokens, for_add=False, for_context=False, for_modify=False, allow_template=True):
    q = Query()
    summary = []
    note_words = []
    in_note = False
    priority_seen = False
    for tok in tokens:
        if tok == "--":
            q.ignore_context = True
            continue
        if for_add and tok == "/":
            in_note = True
            continue
        if in_note:
            note_words.append(tok)
            continue
        if allow_template and tok.startswith("template:"):
            try:
                q.template_id = int(tok.split(':',1)[1])
            except Exception:
                q.template_id = -1
            continue
        if tok.startswith("due:"):
            val = tok.split(':',1)[1]
            try:
                q.due = parse_due_token(val)
            except ValueError:
                raise
            continue
        if tok in PRIORITIES and not priority_seen:
            q.priority = tok
            priority_seen = True
            continue
        if tok.startswith("+") and len(tok) > 1:
            q.tags.append(tok[1:])
            continue
        if tok.startswith("-project:"):
            val = tok.split(':',1)[1]
            if val:
                q.antiprojects.append(val)
            continue
        if tok.startswith("project:"):
            # project: with empty value is an operation only in add (clear/default); as a filter it is no-op.
            q.project = tok.split(':',1)[1]
            continue
        if tok.startswith("-") and len(tok) > 1:
            q.antitags.append(tok[1:])
            continue
        summary.append(tok)
    q.tags = sorted_unique(q.tags)
    q.antitags = sorted_unique(q.antitags)
    q.antiprojects = sorted_unique(q.antiprojects)
    q.text = " ".join(summary)
    q.note = " ".join(note_words)
    if for_context and q.text:
        raise RuntimeError("context cannot contain text")
    return q


def due_parse_error(val):
    eprint_red(f"Invalid due date format: {val}\nExpected format: YYYY-MM-DD, MM-DD or DD, relative date like 'next-monday', 'today', etc.")


def context_file(repo):
    return state_dir(repo) / "context.txt"


def get_context(repo):
    env = os.environ.get("DSTASK_CONTEXT")
    if env is not None:
        return env.strip()
    p = context_file(repo)
    if p.exists():
        return p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    return ""


def set_context(repo, ctx):
    p = context_file(repo)
    if ctx:
        p.write_text(ctx, encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        try: p.unlink()
        except FileNotFoundError: pass


def context_query(repo):
    ctx = get_context(repo)
    if not ctx:
        return Query()
    try:
        return parse_tokens(ctx.split(), for_context=True, allow_template=False)
    except Exception:
        return Query()


def apply_context_to_new(t: Task, cq: Query):
    t.tags = sorted_unique(list(t.tags) + cq.tags)
    if cq.project:
        t.project = cq.project
    if cq.priority:
        t.priority = cq.priority
    if cq.due:
        t.due = cq.due


def task_matches(t: Task, q: Query):
    tags = set(t.tags)
    for tag in q.tags:
        if tag not in tags:
            return False
    for tag in q.antitags:
        if tag in tags:
            return False
    if q.project:
        if t.project != q.project:
            return False
    for p in q.antiprojects:
        if t.project == p:
            return False
    if q.priority:
        if t.priority != q.priority:
            return False
    if q.due:
        if t.due != q.due:
            return False
    if q.text:
        hay = (t.summary or "") + "\n" + (t.notes or "")
        if q.text not in hay:
            return False
    return True


def combine_queries(a: Query, b: Query):
    q = Query()
    q.tags = sorted_unique(a.tags + b.tags)
    q.antitags = sorted_unique(a.antitags + b.antitags)
    q.project = b.project or a.project
    q.antiprojects = sorted_unique(a.antiprojects + b.antiprojects)
    q.priority = b.priority or a.priority
    q.due = b.due or a.due
    q.text = b.text or a.text
    return q


def is_tty():
    return bool(os.environ.get("DSTASK_FAKE_PTY")) or sys.stdout.isatty()


def print_json_tasks(tasks):
    objs = [t.to_json_obj() for t in tasks]
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(objs, indent=2))


def visible_width(s):
    return len(s)


def row_color(t: Task):
    if t.status == "active":
        return "\033[0;38;5;233;48;5;250m"
    if t.status == "paused":
        return "\033[0;38;5;250;48;5;236m"
    return {
        "P0": "\033[0;38;5;160;48;5;232m",
        "P1": "\033[0;38;5;166;48;5;233m",
        "P2": "\033[0;38;5;250;48;5;233m",
        "P3": "\033[0;38;5;245;48;5;232m",
    }.get(t.priority, "\033[0;38;5;250;48;5;233m")


def fmt_due(t):
    d = parse_rfc_date(t.due)
    if not d:
        return ""
    return d.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def print_table(tasks):
    width = 80
    # ID(4) Priority(10) Tags(6) Due(5) Project(9) Summary(rest)
    header = f"{'ID':<4}{'Priority':<10}{'Tags':<6}{'Due':<5}{'Project':<9}Summary"
    header = header[:width].ljust(width)
    print(f"\033[4;38;5;250;48;5;232m{header}{RESET}")
    for t in tasks:
        tags = ",".join(t.tags)
        due = fmt_due(t)
        prefix = f"{t.id:<4}{t.priority:<10}{tags:<6}{due:<5}{t.project:<9}"
        summ_width = max(0, width - len(prefix))
        summary = t.summary[:summ_width].ljust(summ_width)
        line = (prefix + summary)[:width].ljust(width)
        print(f"{row_color(t)}{line}{RESET}")
    print(f"\n{len(tasks)} tasks.")


def output_tasks(tasks):
    if is_tty():
        print_table(tasks)
    else:
        print_json_tasks(tasks)


def find_by_id(tasks, idnum, include_templates=True, open_only=False):
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id == idnum and t.status in LIVE_STATUSES:
            if open_only and t.status not in OPEN_STATUSES:
                continue
            if not include_templates and t.status == "template":
                continue
            return t
    return None


def task_ids_from_args(args):
    ids = []
    rest = []
    for a in args:
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d+", a):
            ids.append(int(a))
        else:
            rest.append(a)
    return ids, rest


def parse_command(argv):
    # Return command, ids, remaining args. Commands and IDs can be swapped; unknowns are filters for next.
    if not argv:
        return "next", [], []
    if argv[0] == "help":
        return "help", [], argv[1:]
    # first command occurrence wins
    cmd_index = None
    cmd = None
    for i,a in enumerate(argv):
        if a in COMMANDS and a not in ("_completions",):
            cmd_index = i; cmd = a; break
    if cmd is None:
        return "next", [], argv
    before = argv[:cmd_index]
    after = argv[cmd_index+1:]
    ids = []
    # IDs before command always IDs.
    for a in before:
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d+", a):
            ids.append(int(a))
        else:
            # Non-ID before command makes the whole thing a filter unless command was first.
            if cmd_index != 0:
                return "next", [], argv
    # For ID-taking commands, leading numeric args after command are IDs; remaining are text/ops.
    if cmd in ("start","stop","done","resolve","remove","rm","modify","edit","note","notes","open","template"):
        rest = []
        consuming = True
        for a in after:
            if consuming and re.fullmatch(r"\d+", a):
                ids.append(int(a))
            else:
                consuming = False
                rest.append(a)
        after = rest
    return cmd, ids, after


def make_task_from_query(q: Query, status="pending", base: Task=None):
    if base:
        t = Task(uuid=str(uuidlib.uuid4()), status=status, summary=base.summary, notes=base.notes,
                 tags=list(base.tags), project=base.project, priority=base.priority, created=now_rfc3339nano(),
                 resolved=ZERO_TIME, due=base.due)
        if t.notes:
            t.notes = t.notes + "\n"
    else:
        t = Task(uuid=str(uuidlib.uuid4()), status=status, created=now_rfc3339nano())
    if q.text:
        t.summary = q.text
    for tag in q.tags:
        if tag not in t.tags:
            t.tags.append(tag)
    t.tags = sorted_unique(t.tags)
    # q.antitags are ignored for add, matching observed behavior.
    if q.project != "":
        t.project = q.project
    elif any(tok == "project:" for tok in []):
        t.project = ""
    if q.priority:
        t.priority = q.priority
    if q.due:
        t.due = q.due
    if q.note and status != "resolved":
        if t.notes:
            t.notes = t.notes + q.note
        else:
            t.notes = q.note
    return t


def cmd_add(repo, args, start=False, template_mode=False, log_mode=False):
    try:
        q = parse_tokens(args, for_add=True, allow_template=True)
    except ValueError as e:
        due_parse_error(str(e)); return 1
    tasks = load_tasks(repo)
    cq = context_query(repo) if not q.ignore_context else Query()
    ctx_str = get_context(repo) if not q.ignore_context else ""
    if ctx_str and not log_mode:
        print(f"{YELLOW}Active context: {ctx_str}{RESET}")
    base = None
    if q.template_id:
        base = find_by_id(tasks, q.template_id, include_templates=True)
        if not base or base.status != "template":
            eprint_red(f"no template with ID {q.template_id} exists")
            return 1
    if not q.text and not base:
        eprint_red("task description or template required")
        return 1
    status = "pending"
    if start:
        status = "active"
    if template_mode:
        status = "template"
    if log_mode:
        status = "resolved"
    t = make_task_from_query(q, status=status, base=base)
    if not q.ignore_context and not log_mode:
        apply_context_to_new(t, cq)
    if log_mode:
        t.resolved = now_rfc3339nano()
        # observed log ignores slash note
        t.notes = ""
    write_task(repo, t)
    t.id = allocate_id(repo, t.uuid) if t.status in LIVE_STATUSES else 0
    if log_mode:
        msg = f"Logged {t.summary}"
    elif template_mode:
        msg = f"Created Template {t.id}: {t.summary}"
    elif start:
        msg = f"Added and started {t.id}: {t.summary}"
    else:
        msg = f"Added {t.id}: {t.summary}"
    print(f"\n{msg}")
    rc = commit_all(repo, msg)
    return 0 if rc == 0 else 1


def append_note_stop_done(t: Task, text: str):
    if text:
        t.notes = (t.notes or "") + "\n" + text


def transition(repo, ids, args, target):
    tasks = load_tasks(repo)
    if not ids:
        eprint_red("no ID(s) specified")
        return 1
    rc = 0
    text = " ".join(args)
    for idnum in ids:
        tasks = load_tasks(repo)
        t = find_by_id(tasks, idnum, include_templates=False, open_only=True)
        if not t:
            eprint_red(f"no open task with ID {idnum} exists")
            rc = 1; continue
        oldstatus = t.status
        if target == "active":
            if oldstatus == "active":
                eprint_red("invalid state transition: active -> active")
                rc = 1; continue
            t.status = "active"
            msg = f"Started {t.id}: {t.summary}"
        elif target == "paused":
            if oldstatus != "active":
                eprint_red(f"invalid state transition: {oldstatus} -> paused")
                rc = 1; continue
            t.status = "paused"
            append_note_stop_done(t, text)
            msg = f"Stopped {t.id}: {t.summary}"
        elif target == "resolved":
            t.status = "resolved"
            t.resolved = now_rfc3339nano()
            append_note_stop_done(t, text)
            msg = f"Resolved {t.id}: {t.summary}"
        write_task(repo, t)
        if target == "resolved":
            remove_id(repo, t.uuid)
        print(f"\n{msg}")
        c = commit_all(repo, msg)
        if c != 0: rc = 1
        if target == "active" and t.notes:
            print(f"\nNotes on task {t.id}:")
            print(f"{GREY}{t.notes}{RESET}\n")
    return rc


def cmd_remove(repo, ids):
    tasks = load_tasks(repo)
    if not ids:
        eprint_red("no ID(s) specified")
        return 1
    rc = 0
    for idnum in ids:
        tasks = load_tasks(repo)
        t = find_by_id(tasks, idnum, include_templates=True)
        if not t:
            eprint_red(f"no task with ID {idnum} exists")
            rc = 1; continue
        print(f"{t.id}: {t.summary}")
        try:
            Path(t.path).unlink()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        remove_id(repo, t.uuid)
        msg = f"Removed: {t.id}: {t.summary}"
        print(f"\n{msg}")
        c = commit_all(repo, msg)
        if c != 0: rc = 1
    return rc


def cmd_template(repo, ids, args):
    # If an ID is supplied, observed behavior changes that task to a template and ignores modification args.
    if ids:
        tasks = load_tasks(repo)
        rc = 0
        for idnum in ids:
            tasks = load_tasks(repo)
            t = find_by_id(tasks, idnum, include_templates=False, open_only=True)
            if not t:
                eprint_red(f"no open task with ID {idnum} exists")
                rc = 1; continue
            t.status = "template"
            write_task(repo, t)
            msg = f"Changed {t.id}: {t.summary} to Template"
            print(f"\n{msg}")
            c = commit_all(repo, msg)
            if c != 0: rc = 1
        return rc
    return cmd_add(repo, args, template_mode=True)


def apply_modify(t: Task, q: Query):
    changed_ops = False
    for tag in q.tags:
        changed_ops = True
        if tag not in t.tags:
            t.tags.append(tag)
    for tag in q.antitags:
        changed_ops = True
        t.tags = [x for x in t.tags if x != tag]
    if q.project:
        changed_ops = True
        t.project = q.project
    for p in q.antiprojects:
        changed_ops = True
        if t.project == p:
            t.project = ""
    if q.priority:
        changed_ops = True
        t.priority = q.priority
    if q.due:
        changed_ops = True
        t.due = q.due
    t.tags = sorted_unique(t.tags)
    return changed_ops


def cmd_modify(repo, ids, args):
    try:
        q = parse_tokens(args, for_modify=True, allow_template=False)
    except ValueError as e:
        due_parse_error(str(e)); return 1
    if not (q.tags or q.antitags or q.project or q.antiprojects or q.priority or q.due):
        eprint_red("no operations specified")
        return 1
    tasks = load_tasks(repo)
    if not ids:
        cq = context_query(repo)
        targets = [t for t in sort_tasks(tasks) if t.status in OPEN_STATUSES and task_matches(t, cq)]
    else:
        targets = []
        for idnum in ids:
            t = find_by_id(tasks, idnum, include_templates=False, open_only=True)
            if not t:
                eprint_red(f"no open task with ID {idnum} exists")
            else:
                targets.append(t)
    rc = 0
    for target in targets:
        tasks = load_tasks(repo)
        t = next((x for x in tasks if x.uuid == target.uuid), target)
        apply_modify(t, q)
        write_task(repo, t)
        msg = f"Modified {t.id}: {t.summary}"
        print(f"\n{msg}")
        c = commit_all(repo, msg)
        if c != 0: rc = 1
    return rc


def cmd_context(repo, args):
    if not args:
        print(get_context(repo))
        return 0
    if args == ["none"] or args == ["--"]:
        set_context(repo, "")
        return 0
    try:
        q = parse_tokens(args, for_context=True, allow_template=False)
    except ValueError as e:
        due_parse_error(str(e)); return 1
    except RuntimeError as e:
        eprint_red(str(e)); return 1
    set_context(repo, " ".join([a for a in args if a != "--"]))
    return 0


def cmd_list(repo, cmd, args):
    try:
        q = parse_tokens(args, allow_template=False)
    except ValueError as e:
        due_parse_error(str(e)); return 1
    tasks = load_tasks(repo)
    if cmd in ("next", "show-next"):
        base = [t for t in tasks if t.status in OPEN_STATUSES]
    elif cmd == "show-open":
        base = [t for t in tasks if t.status in OPEN_STATUSES]
    elif cmd == "show-active":
        base = [t for t in tasks if t.status == "active"]
    elif cmd == "show-paused":
        base = [t for t in tasks if t.status == "paused"]
    elif cmd == "show-resolved":
        base = [t for t in tasks if t.status == "resolved"]
    elif cmd == "show-templates":
        base = [t for t in tasks if t.status == "template"]
    elif cmd == "show-unorganised":
        base = [t for t in tasks if t.status in OPEN_STATUSES and not t.tags and not t.project]
        q.ignore_context = True
    else:
        base = [t for t in tasks if t.status in OPEN_STATUSES]
    if not q.ignore_context and cmd != "show-unorganised":
        q = combine_queries(context_query(repo), q)
    filtered = [t for t in base if task_matches(t, q)]
    output_tasks(sort_tasks(filtered))
    return 0


def cmd_show_tags(repo):
    tasks = load_tasks(repo)
    seen = []
    # Original effectively follows filesystem path order for open tasks.
    for t in sorted([x for x in tasks if x.status in OPEN_STATUSES], key=lambda x: str(x.path)):
        for tag in t.tags:
            if tag not in seen:
                seen.append(tag)
    for tag in seen:
        print(tag)
    return 0


def cmd_show_projects(repo):
    tasks = load_tasks(repo)
    projects = {}
    for t in tasks:
        if not t.project:
            continue
        p = projects.setdefault(t.project, [])
        p.append(t)
    res = []
    prio_order = {p:i for i,p in enumerate(PRIORITIES)}
    for name, ts in projects.items():
        created = min([x.created for x in ts], key=parse_time_key)
        resolved_tasks = [x for x in ts if x.status == "resolved"]
        resolved = ZERO_TIME
        if resolved_tasks and len(resolved_tasks) == len(ts):
            resolved = max([x.resolved for x in resolved_tasks], key=parse_time_key)
        elif resolved_tasks:
            resolved = max([x.resolved for x in resolved_tasks], key=parse_time_key)
        open_ts = [x for x in ts if x.status in OPEN_STATUSES]
        active = any(x.status == "active" for x in ts)
        priority = "P2"
        if open_ts:
            priority = sorted([x.priority for x in open_ts], key=lambda p: prio_order.get(p,2))[0]
        res.append({
            "name": name,
            "taskCount": len(ts),
            "resolvedCount": len(resolved_tasks),
            "active": active,
            "created": created,
            "resolved": resolved,
            "priority": priority,
        })
    res.sort(key=lambda x: (prio_order.get(x["priority"],2), parse_time_key(x["created"]), x["name"]))
    if is_tty():
        header = f"{'Name':<6}{'Progress':<10}{'Created':<14}"
        print(f"\033[4;38;5;250;48;5;232m{header}{RESET}")
        for p in res:
            d = parse_rfc_date(p["created"])
            ds = d.strftime("%a %-d %b %Y") if d else ""
            line = f"{p['name']:<6}{(str(p['resolvedCount'])+'/'+str(p['taskCount'])):<10}{ds:<14}"
            bg = "232" if p['resolvedCount'] == 0 else "233"
            print(f"\033[0;38;5;250;48;5;{bg}m{line}{RESET}")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(res, indent=2))
    return 0


def cmd_note(repo, ids, args):
    # Observed: in non-TTY note does nothing (even with text). In TTY/fake PTY it edits/appends.
    if not is_tty():
        return 0
    tasks = load_tasks(repo)
    if not ids:
        eprint_red("no ID(s) specified")
        return 1
    rc = 0
    text = " ".join(args)
    for idnum in ids:
        tasks = load_tasks(repo)
        t = find_by_id(tasks, idnum, include_templates=True)
        if not t:
            eprint_red(f"no open task with ID {idnum} exists")
            rc = 1; continue
        if text:
            if t.notes:
                t.notes += "\n" + text
            else:
                t.notes = text
        else:
            editor = os.environ.get("EDITOR") or os.environ.get("VISUAL") or "vi"
            safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "-", t.summary).strip('-') or "task"
            tmp = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"dstask.{os.getpid()}.{t.id}-{safe}.md"
            tmp.write_text(t.notes or "", encoding="utf-8")
            subprocess.run([editor, str(tmp)])
            try:
                t.notes = tmp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            except Exception:
                pass
            try: tmp.unlink()
            except Exception: pass
        write_task(repo, t)
        msg = f"Edit note {t.id}: {t.summary}"
        print(f"\n{msg}")
        c = commit_all(repo, msg)
        if c != 0: rc = 1
    return rc


def task_to_edit_yaml(t: Task):
    lines = [f"status: {t.status}\n"]
    # reuse writer into temp-like content
    dummy_repo = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    try:
        write_task(dummy_repo, t)
        content = (dummy_repo / t.status / f"{t.uuid}.yml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        lines.extend(content.splitlines(True))
        return "".join(lines)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(str(dummy_repo), ignore_errors=True)


def parse_edit_content(content, old: Task):
    tmpdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    try:
        p = tmpdir / f"{old.uuid}.yml"
        p.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
        t = parse_task_file(p, old.status)
        t.uuid = old.uuid
        t.id = old.id
        t.path = old.path
        if t.status not in LIVE_STATUSES and t.status != "resolved":
            t.status = old.status
        return t
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(str(tmpdir), ignore_errors=True)


def cmd_edit(repo, ids):
    if not ids:
        eprint_red("no ID(s) specified")
        return 1
    rc = 0
    for idnum in ids:
        tasks = load_tasks(repo)
        t = find_by_id(tasks, idnum, include_templates=True)
        if not t:
            eprint_red(f"no task with ID {idnum} exists")
            rc = 1; continue
        editor = os.environ.get("EDITOR") or os.environ.get("VISUAL") or "vi"
        tmp = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"dstask-edit-{os.getpid()}-{t.id}.yml"
        tmp.write_text(task_to_edit_yaml(t), encoding="utf-8")
        subprocess.run([editor, str(tmp)])
        try:
            new = parse_edit_content(tmp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), t)
        except Exception:
            new = t
        try: tmp.unlink()
        except Exception: pass
        if new.status != t.status:
            new.path = t.path
        write_task(repo, new)
        msg = f"Edited {new.id}: {new.summary}"
        print(f"\n{msg}")
        c = commit_all(repo, msg)
        if c != 0: rc = 1
    return rc


def cmd_open(repo, ids):
    if not ids:
        eprint_red("no ID(s) specified")
        return 1
    tasks = load_tasks(repo)
    rc = 0
    url_re = re.compile(r"https?://[^\s)>"]+")
    for idnum in ids:
        t = find_by_id(tasks, idnum, include_templates=True)
        if not t:
            eprint_red(f"no open task with ID {idnum} exists")
            rc = 1; continue
        urls = url_re.findall((t.summary or "") + "\n" + (t.notes or ""))
        urls = [u.rstrip('.,;') for u in urls]
        if not urls:
            eprint_red(f"no URLs found in task {idnum}")
            rc = 1; continue
        opener = shutil.which("xdg-open") or shutil.which("open")
        if not opener:
            eprint_red("Failed to open browser")
            rc = 1; continue
        for u in urls:
            p = subprocess.run([opener, u], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            if p.returncode != 0:
                eprint_red("Failed to open browser")
                rc = 1
                break
    return rc


def cmd_undo(repo, args):
    if len(args) > 1:
        print(HELP_TEXTS["undo"], end="")
        return 0
    if len(args) == 0:
        rev = "HEAD"
    else:
        try:
            n = int(args[0])
        except Exception:
            print(HELP_TEXTS["undo"], end="")
            return 0
        if n <= 1:
            rev = "HEAD"
        else:
            rev = f"HEAD~{n}.."
    return run_git_passthrough(repo, ["revert", "--no-edit", rev])


def cmd_sync(repo):
    rc = run_git_passthrough(repo, ["pull"])
    if rc != 0:
        return rc
    return run_git_passthrough(repo, ["push"])


def cmd_completions(repo, args):
    # The completion engine prints candidates matching the current word.
    candidates = [
        "next", "add", "rm", "remove", "template", "log", "start", "note", "notes", "stop",
        "done", "resolve", "context", "modify", "edit", "undo", "sync", "open", "git",
        "show-next", "show-projects", "show-tags", "show-active", "show-paused", "show-open",
        "show-resolved", "show-templates", "show-unorganised", "bash-completion", "fish-completion",
        "zsh-completion", "help", "version", "P0", "P1", "P2", "P3",
    ]
    try:
        tasks = load_tasks(repo)
        projects = []
        tags = []
        for t in tasks:
            if t.status in OPEN_STATUSES or t.status == "template":
                if t.project and t.project not in projects:
                    projects.append(t.project)
                for tag in t.tags:
                    if tag not in tags:
                        tags.append(tag)
        for p in sorted(projects):
            candidates += [f"project:{p}", f"-project:{p}"]
        for tag in sorted(tags, reverse=True):
            candidates += [f"+{tag}", f"-{tag}"]
    except Exception:
        pass
    prefix = ""
    if args:
        # If called from shell wrappers, first arg is program name and last is current word.
        prefix = args[-1]
    for c in candidates:
        if c.startswith(prefix):
            print(c)
    return 0


def main(argv):
    if argv and argv[0] == "version":
        print("Version: Unknown")
        print("Git commit: Unknown")
        print("Build date: Unknown")
        return 0
    if argv and argv[0] == "help":
        if len(argv) > 1 and argv[1] in HELP_TEXTS:
            print(HELP_TEXTS[argv[1]], end="")
        else:
            print(HELP_SUMMARY, end="")
        return 0
    if argv and argv[0] == "bash-completion":
        print(BASH_COMPLETION, end="")
        return 0
    if argv and argv[0] == "zsh-completion":
        print(ZSH_COMPLETION, end="")
        return 0
    if argv and argv[0] == "fish-completion":
        print(FISH_COMPLETION, end="")
        return 0

    # Hidden completions needs repo for dynamic candidates; it also works if repo must be initialized.
    repo = ensure_repo()
    if argv and argv[0] == "_completions":
        return cmd_completions(repo, argv[1:])

    cmd, ids, args = parse_command(argv)
    if cmd == "rm": cmd = "remove"
    if cmd == "resolve": cmd = "done"
    if cmd == "notes": cmd = "note"
    if cmd == "show-next": cmd = "next"

    if cmd == "version":
        print("Version: Unknown"); print("Git commit: Unknown"); print("Build date: Unknown"); return 0
    if cmd == "add": return cmd_add(repo, args)
    if cmd == "template": return cmd_template(repo, ids, args)
    if cmd == "log": return cmd_add(repo, args, log_mode=True)
    if cmd == "start":
        if ids:
            return transition(repo, ids, args, "active")
        return cmd_add(repo, args, start=True)
    if cmd == "stop": return transition(repo, ids, args, "paused")
    if cmd == "done": return transition(repo, ids, args, "resolved")
    if cmd == "remove": return cmd_remove(repo, ids)
    if cmd == "modify": return cmd_modify(repo, ids, args)
    if cmd == "context": return cmd_context(repo, args)
    if cmd in ("next","show-open","show-active","show-paused","show-resolved","show-templates","show-unorganised"):
        return cmd_list(repo, cmd, args)
    if cmd == "show-tags": return cmd_show_tags(repo)
    if cmd == "show-projects": return cmd_show_projects(repo)
    if cmd == "note": return cmd_note(repo, ids, args)
    if cmd == "edit": return cmd_edit(repo, ids)
    if cmd == "open": return cmd_open(repo, ids)
    if cmd == "git": return run_git_passthrough(repo, args)
    if cmd == "undo": return cmd_undo(repo, args)
    if cmd == "sync": return cmd_sync(repo)
    # Fallback: default list with all argv as filter.
    return cmd_list(repo, "next", argv)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
    except BrokenPipeError:
        try:
            sys.stdout.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        sys.exit(0)
